title: Managing Successful Projects With PRINCE2 test prep

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the ‘Project Initiation Document’ (PID)?
answers: To document the details of all lessons learned during the project lifecycle.
To provide detailed instructions for the project team on how to complete tasks.
To provide a baseline plan for the project, outlining its scope, goals and objectives.
To detail the technical specifications for all of the project's deliverables.
feedbacks: Lessons learned are not recorded in the PID.
Instructions for tasks are managed in work packages.
This accurately describes the purpose of the PID.
Technical specifications are not managed in the PID.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Initiation Document’ provides an outline of the project, and sets the baseline that will be used to manage the project and ensure successful delivery.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of 'Product Descriptions'?
answers: To document the project's business case, objectives, and success criteria.
To provide detailed technical specifications and quality criteria for specific project products.
To outline the project's risk management approach and mitigation strategies.
To detail how communications should be managed throughout the project with all stakeholders.
feedbacks: Project objectives are not defined in product descriptions.
This is the correct description of product descriptions.
Risk management is not the focus of the product description.
Stakeholder communications are managed separately.
questions.explanation: ‘Product Descriptions’ specify the technical characteristics of a project deliverable, and outline the standards it must meet.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing a high number of change requests which are impacting on project progress, what is the best first action for the project manager to take?
answers: Demand that the project board provide an immediate freeze on all change requests.
Immediately reject all incoming change requests to keep the project on track.
Review the change management process and ensure it is being followed correctly.
Ignore the change requests and continue to work towards completing the project plan.
feedbacks: Demanding a freeze is not the best approach.
Rejecting all changes without assessment is not good practice.
This is the most appropriate first action.
Ignoring changes is not appropriate project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager should ensure the change management process is correct, and followed fully, before attempting to action any changes.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the PRINCE2 principle of 'Tailor to suit the project environment'?
answers: Project boards should adapt the project management style to suit the project team’s preferences.
Project teams should be allowed to choose the style of management and processes that suit them.
Projects should use only the PRINCE2 process that are deemed necessary and beneficial.
Projects should be managed in a rigid format without any adaptation to specific circumstances.
feedbacks: Adapting to team preferences is not the focus of this principle.
Team choice of process is not a feature of this principle.
This accurately describes the tailor to suit principle.
Rigid format is not a feature of this principle.
questions.explanation: ‘Tailor to Suit the Project Environment’ dictates that all project plans should be modified and tailored to meet the specific requirements of that project.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY role of the 'Senior User' on the Project Board?
answers: To provide the project with specialist resources and technical advice.
To represent the interests and needs of those who will use the project's products.
To manage the project budget and ensure all financial resources are properly allocated.
To manage all day-to-day project activity, and ensure the project delivers on time and to budget.
feedbacks: Technical advice is provided by the senior supplier.
This is the primary role of the senior user.
Budget management is the responsibility of the project executive.
Day to day management is the responsibility of the project manager.
questions.explanation: The ‘Senior User’ represents the needs of the end user of the project’s deliverables and ensures that their perspective is considered in the management of the project.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has a large number of risks recorded on the risk register what is the first action the project manager should take?
answers: Delegate responsibility for managing the risks to a project support team member.
Immediately implement a project-wide risk management and mitigation strategy.
Meet with the project team to review the risk register and identify high impact risks.
Ignore all of the risks and proceed as planned with project delivery.
feedbacks: Delegating risk to support is not appropriate.
Implementing strategies without review is not correct.
Reviewing the register is the most appropriate first step.
Ignoring risks is not good practice.
questions.explanation: The project manager must review all of the risks with the project team in order to identify and mitigate any potential high impact risks.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical component of a PRINCE2 ‘Quality Management Approach’ document?
answers: The method of measuring product quality against defined standards.
The individuals who will be responsible for quality control activities.
The processes and timescales required to complete all project tasks.
The techniques used to ensure quality of all deliverables.
feedbacks: Measuring quality is a key feature of this document.
Quality control responsibility is a part of the document.
Project timescales are not a component of this document.
Quality techniques are a feature of this document.
questions.explanation: The ‘Quality Management Approach’ defines how project deliverables will meet quality standards, and not the timescales required to complete the tasks.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term ‘Tolerance’ specifically define?
answers: The acceptable level of risk that the project team is willing to take.
The level of flexibility that can be applied to the project timeline.
The agreed limits of acceptable deviation from the planned baselines.
The level of conflict that the project team can withstand without impacting progress.
feedbacks: Risk appetite is separate from tolerance.
Flexibility of timescales is not the only focus of tolerance.
This is the definition of tolerance.
Team conflict is not the focus of the tolerance definition.
questions.explanation: ‘Tolerance’ defines the permissible variation from the project’s cost, scope, quality, risk, time and benefit baselines.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team is experiencing low morale, and a lack of motivation from team members. What is the BEST action for the Project Manager to take FIRST?
answers: Publicly reprimand all team members who are not contributing to the project.
Reassign all team members to different roles, to try and stimulate interest.
Meet with the team to understand the root causes of the morale issues and develop a solution.
Ignore the problem and continue with the project as planned, in the hope it improves.
feedbacks: Public reprimands are not a good approach.
Reassigning roles is not the best approach.
This is the best action to take.
Ignoring the problem is not good practice.
questions.explanation: The project manager must meet with the project team to understand the causes of the issues, and to develop a plan of action to improve team morale.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the 'Directing a Project' process?
answers: To manage all day to day tasks and activities performed by the project team.
To track and monitor project progress against its plans and objectives.
To provide overall direction and control of the project by the project board.
To ensure that all project deliverables meet the required quality standards.
feedbacks: Day to day tasks are managed by the project manager and team.
Progress tracking is managed separately.
This is the core purpose of the Directing a project process.
Product quality is managed separately.
questions.explanation: The ‘Directing a Project’ process ensures that the project remains aligned with the business goals and that the project board has the required information to maintain overall control.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical use of the 'Project Plan' in PRINCE2?
answers: To detail the technical specifications of the products to be delivered.
To schedule all project activities, resources, and milestones.
To provide a baseline against which to monitor project performance.
To define how the project will achieve its objectives and meet stakeholders needs.
feedbacks: Technical specifications are not part of the project plan.
Scheduling project activities is part of the plan.
Providing a baseline is a key feature of the plan.
Defining objectives is a key feature of the project plan.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Plan’ outlines the strategy for delivering project objectives, but does not include technical specifications for project deliverables.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the primary responsibility of the 'Change Authority'?
answers: To manage day-to-day project activities, and ensure the project is delivered on time.
To manage and track all of the projects risks and potential issues.
To manage and decide on all proposed changes to the project scope and plans.
To provide guidance on technical issues that may arise during the project.
feedbacks: Day to day management is not the responsibility of the change authority.
Risk and issue management are managed by other roles.
This is the primary role of the change authority.
Technical guidance is provided by a separate role.
questions.explanation: The ‘Change Authority’ is responsible for reviewing, assessing and making decisions on any requests for changes to the project baselines and plans.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project manager is finding it difficult to manage the project workload and is feeling overwhelmed. What action should the project board take FIRST?
answers: Immediately replace the project manager with a more experienced resource.
Demand that the project manager improve performance or face disciplinary action.
Review the project's plan and assess where additional support can be provided.
Instruct the project manager to work extra hours to ensure the project is delivered on time.
feedbacks: Replacing immediately is not the first step to take.
Demanding performance is not an appropriate approach.
Reviewing the plan is the best first action.
Instructing extra hours is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: The project board should review the project and work with the manager to identify areas where support or resources can assist in delivering the project.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of the 'Lessons Learned Report' in PRINCE2?
answers: To record all risks and issues that occurred during the project lifecycle.
To capture the performance of the project team during project delivery.
To provide a documented record of experiences to benefit future projects.
To provide a detailed analysis of the project’s overall financial performance.
feedbacks: Risks and issues are recorded elsewhere.
Team performance is not the purpose of the report.
This accurately describes the purpose of the lessons learned report.
Project financial performance is documented elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The ‘Lessons Learned Report’ is a record of the experiences and outcomes of the project that will be used to inform the management of future projects.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the main purpose of the 'Managing Product Delivery' process?
answers: To manage all resources and activities needed to achieve the project’s objectives.
To plan and control the execution of work assigned to project teams.
To monitor project progress against schedule, and manage project finances.
To provide governance and direction for the overall project delivery.
feedbacks: The resources needed are managed elsewhere.
This accurately describes the managing product delivery process.
Managing finances is not the purpose of this process.
Governance is provided by other project board functions.
questions.explanation: The ‘Managing Product Delivery’ process controls the work that is performed by specialist teams to ensure they deliver project products as planned.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does ‘Product-Based Planning’ primarily ensure?
answers: That all project activity is focused on the timely delivery of all project milestones.
That all project plans are focused on the required deliverables and outcomes.
That project plans are focused on ensuring resources are fully utilized and not wasted.
That all project plans are focused on ensuring a positive return on investment.
feedbacks: Milestone focus is not the purpose of this type of planning.
This is the purpose of product based planning.
Resource utilization is not a key driver of this type of planning.
Return on investment is not the focus of this planning.
questions.explanation: ‘Product-Based Planning’ ensures the project is focused on what is to be delivered and that all activity is structured to produce those products effectively.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team is consistently failing to meet quality standards, what is the BEST action for the project manager to take FIRST?
answers: Publicly reprimand the team and demand they improve standards immediately.
Reassign the work to a smaller team with a proven track record of quality delivery.
Review the existing quality standards and discuss how the team can improve.
Ignore the issue as the project is being delivered on time and within budget.
feedbacks: Public reprimands are not a good approach.
Reassigning work might not fix the issue.
This is the best first step.
Ignoring quality problems is not good practice.
questions.explanation: The project manager must attempt to understand the causes of quality issues and develop a plan of action with the project team.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role within the PRINCE2 ‘Project Management Team’ structure?
answers: Project Manager
Team Leader
Project Support
Quality Assurance Manager
feedbacks: The project manager is key to project success.
Team leaders are part of the team management structure.
Project support is a common role.
Quality Assurance Manager is not a specific role in the structure.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Management Team’ structure usually contains the Project Manager, Team Leader and support roles, but not a specific quality assurance manager role.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the main purpose of the ‘Communication Management Approach’?
answers: To document all of the financial transactions that have taken place during the project.
To document all of the project’s technical requirements and product specifications.
To provide a strategy for how all information will be communicated with project stakeholders.
To document all of the lessons that have been learned during the course of the project.
feedbacks: Financial transactions are not documented in the communications approach.
Technical specifications are not part of the communications approach.
This is the correct description of the communications approach.
Lessons learned are managed separately.
questions.explanation: The ‘Communication Management Approach’ outlines how project communications will be managed and delivered to all stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term 'Exception' specifically refer to?
answers: A project that has been completed early and under budget, exceeding all initial targets.
A change request that has been approved by the change authority, but will require additional resources.
A situation where a project has deviated beyond its agreed tolerances.
A significant event that is anticipated, and can be easily resolved with the current resource plan.
feedbacks: Meeting all targets is not an exception.
Change requests are handled separately.
This is the correct definition of an exception.
An easily resolved issue is not an exception.
questions.explanation: An ‘Exception’ is when the project goes outside of agreed tolerance limits, requiring the escalation of the issue and creation of an exception plan.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the PRINCE2 principle of ‘Manage by Stages’?
answers: Projects should be planned and managed as one single continuous phase from initiation through to completion.
Projects should be planned and managed in a series of discrete, controllable stages.
Project management should be devolved to the project team, who can decide how work is to be delivered.
Projects should be planned using a rigid structure that cannot be changed once the project has started.
feedbacks: Managing as a single phase is not a key part of this principle.
This is the correct approach of manage by stages.
Delegation of management is a separate concept.
Rigid structure is not a key part of this principle.
questions.explanation: ‘Manage by Stages’ ensures that projects are broken down into manageable and controllable phases that provide opportunities for assessment and authorization.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the best first action a project manager should take when a significant risk is identified?
answers: Immediately start to implement the risk mitigation strategy for the risk.
Ignore the risk and hope that it is not likely to occur during the project.
Escalate the risk to the project board with an assessment of impact and options.
Start a new risk management plan to include the newly identified risks.
feedbacks: Implementing mitigation before escalation is not good practice.
Ignoring risk is not good project management.
Escalating the risk is the correct first step.
Starting a new plan without review is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: The project manager must escalate all significant risks to the project board, and provide them with an assessment of its impact and any proposed mitigation options.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical element of a PRINCE2 ‘Work Package’?
answers: A description of the project’s overall goals, objectives and business case.
A clear description of the work to be completed and the product to be delivered.
The quality criteria that the deliverable must adhere to.
The resources and skills required to complete the tasks.
feedbacks: The overall goals are separate to the work package.
A description of work is a key feature of the work package.
Quality criteria is a key element of the work package.
Resources and skills are part of the work package information.
questions.explanation: The ‘Work Package’ details specific tasks, products and skills required for delivery, but does not include overall project goals, and business cases.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary responsibility of the ‘Project Executive’ on the Project Board?
answers: To ensure that all project deliverables meet the required quality standards.
To manage the project budget and ensure the project delivers value for money.
To manage the project team and provide day to day direction and instruction.
To provide the project with specialist resources and technical advice.
feedbacks: Quality is not the responsibility of the project executive.
This accurately describes the purpose of the executive role.
Day to day management is the responsibility of the project manager.
Technical advice is the role of the senior supplier.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Executive’ is the owner of the project, and is responsible for ensuring that the project has sufficient funding and is delivered with best value for money.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the primary purpose of the 'Benefits Management Plan'?
answers: To provide an analysis of the potential risks the project may face and their required responses.
To detail how and when the project benefits will be measured and realised by the business.
To manage the financial transactions and expenditure during the project’s lifecycle.
To provide a detailed set of instructions for the project team to perform their tasks effectively.
feedbacks: Risk management is managed elsewhere not in the benefits management plan.
This describes the purpose of the benefits management plan.
Financial expenditure is not the focus of the benefits plan.
Task instructions are included in work packages, not benefits management.
questions.explanation: The ‘Benefits Management Plan’ details how the project benefits will be measured, delivered and realized by the business, and when this will occur.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team are failing to follow correct processes and are constantly delivering poor quality work. What action should the project manager take FIRST?
answers: Immediately replace the team members with those that are more experienced.
Publicly reprimand the team for failing to follow the correct processes.
Review the existing processes and meet with the team to discuss how they can improve.
Ignore the issues and hope that the team will eventually start to follow the correct procedures.
feedbacks: Replacing without review is not best practice.
Public reprimands are not a good approach.
Reviewing process and involving the team is the best first step.
Ignoring the issue is not good project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager must attempt to understand why the processes are not being followed, and must work with the team to improve compliance and quality.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of ‘Project Support’ within a PRINCE2 project?
answers: Project Support is used to make key strategic decisions about project delivery.
Project support is used to manage all day to day activity and delegate tasks to team members.
Project support is used to provide administrative assistance to the project manager and team.
Project support is used to provide specialist expertise and technical knowledge to all project teams.
feedbacks: Strategic decisions are made by the project board, not project support.
Task management is performed by the project manager and team leaders.
This describes the purpose of the project support role.
Technical support is provided by other roles.
questions.explanation: ‘Project Support’ provides administrative, planning and project management assistance to the project manager and team.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the main purpose of the ‘Risk Management Approach’ document?
answers: To provide a detailed plan for managing project budgets and financial performance.
To outline how project risks will be identified, managed and controlled.
To define the overall project communication strategy with all project stakeholders.
To document the technical specifications and standards for all project deliverables.
feedbacks: Budget management is separate to the risk management plan.
This is the core purpose of the risk management approach.
Communication is documented elsewhere.
Technical specifications are documented elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The ‘Risk Management Approach’ outlines the planned response to risks and how they will be identified, assessed, controlled, and managed throughout the project.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does 'Configuration Management' mainly focus on?
answers: Managing the interpersonal relations between all of the members of the project team.
Managing all changes to the project’s budget and financial plan.
Managing all of the project's products and deliverables and any changes made to them.
Managing the relationships between the project team and all external stakeholders.
feedbacks: Interpersonal relationships are not part of configuration management.
Budget management is not the role of configuration management.
This is the correct description of configuration management.
Stakeholder management is separate to configuration management.
questions.explanation: ‘Configuration Management’ tracks and controls the project deliverables and their various versions, ensuring a clear history of the project’s progress.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project board has identified that some project deliverables are not meeting the agreed quality standards, what is the best first action for the project board to take?
answers: Demand that the project team immediately re-work all sub-standard deliverables.
Request a full review of the quality management approach and agree how to improve quality.
Remove the team members who are failing to deliver the required quality.
Ignore the low-quality deliverables and focus on completing the project on time and within budget.
feedbacks: Demanding rework without analysis is not appropriate.
This is the best first step.
Removing team members is premature.
Ignoring the issue is not good practice.
questions.explanation: The project board must review the quality management approach and work with the project manager and team to identify how to improve quality levels.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key component of the PRINCE2 ‘Change Theme’?
answers: The process for managing all changes to project timescales.
The process for managing all changes to the project's resources.
The process for defining the project’s specific quality standards.
The process for managing any changes to the agreed project scope.
feedbacks: Managing time changes is part of the change theme.
Managing resource changes is part of the change theme.
Quality standards are defined by the quality theme, not change.
Managing scope changes is part of the change theme.
questions.explanation: The ‘Change Theme’ specifies how changes to a project will be identified, assessed and managed, but is not concerned with setting the project quality standards.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the main purpose of the 'Managing a Stage Boundary' process?
answers: To manage all risks and issues that occur during a particular stage of the project.
To control all day to day project activity and performance against the project plan.
To produce a plan for the next stage of the project and assess progress of the previous stage.
To ensure all project deliverables are produced to the required quality standards.
feedbacks: Risk and issue management is a separate process.
Day to day activity is managed using another process.
This is the purpose of the managing a stage boundary process.
Quality management is not the purpose of the process.
questions.explanation: The ‘Managing a Stage Boundary’ process ensures the project is reviewed at the end of each stage, and a new plan for the next stage is prepared to be reviewed and approved.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term ‘Baseline’ primarily refer to?
answers: The agreed level of risk that the project is willing to accept and manage.
The agreed project plans that will be used as a measure of project progress and control.
The estimated time and resources required to complete all project tasks.
The overall budget that has been allocated for the project by the project board.
feedbacks: Risk appetite is a separate issue to baselines.
This is the core meaning of the baseline.
Estimations of time and resource are a component of plans.
The project budget is managed separately.
questions.explanation: The ‘Baseline’ provides a definitive set of plans against which the project’s performance and progress can be measured and controlled.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is facing a major unexpected technical issue. What action should the Project Manager take FIRST?
answers: Attempt to find a quick technical solution using the resources available to the project team.
Contact the project board and provide them with a summary of the issue and all potential impacts.
Delegate the issue to a junior member of the project team and allow them to try and find a solution.
Ignore the issue and continue to work towards delivering the original project plan.
feedbacks: Attempting a solution without consultation is not best practice.
Contacting the board with a summary of issues is the best action.
Delegating issues without guidance is not appropriate.
Ignoring an issue is not good project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager must escalate any major issue to the project board immediately in order to seek their advice and guidance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical component of the PRINCE2 'Project Plan'?
answers: Details of all key project products and deliverables.
A detailed schedule outlining all tasks, resources and milestones.
The full business case and justification for the project.
The approach that will be taken to manage project risks.
feedbacks: Deliverables are key to a project plan.
Task schedules are key to project plans.
The business case is a separate document from the project plan.
Risk management is an essential component of the project plan.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Plan’ provides details of project timelines, resources, objectives and risks but does not include the detailed business case.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the ‘Lessons Learned Report’?
answers: To provide a summary of the project's overall performance against its agreed objectives.
To record and assess all potential risks and threats that the project could have faced.
To document the overall budget and financial performance of the project.
To record information that could improve future project processes and performance.
feedbacks: Overall performance is included in other documentation.
Risks and threats are managed using a risk register.
Financial performance is not the focus of lessons learned.
This is the correct use of the lessons learned report.
questions.explanation: The ‘Lessons Learned Report’ is designed to capture information about experiences during the project to benefit future projects and improve overall management.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'Exception Plan'?
answers: To document the overall financial performance of the project against the budget.
To provide a revised plan for the project when its tolerances have been exceeded.
To provide a summary of the project performance against the original project objectives.
To provide a detailed report on all potential risks and issues that are facing the project.
feedbacks: Financial performance is not the purpose of the exception plan.
This is the correct purpose of the exception plan.
Project performance is not included in the exception plan.
Risks and issues are not the focus of the exception plan.
questions.explanation: The ‘Exception Plan’ provides a new approach to the delivery of project objectives, when the original plan has exceeded agreed tolerances.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team is consistently delivering products that are not meeting agreed quality standards, what is the BEST action for the project manager to take FIRST?
answers: Immediately implement a plan to reduce the project's scope and objectives.
Issue formal warnings to all team members for not meeting the required standards.
Review the existing quality plan and discuss how to improve quality control with the team.
Reassign the work to a more experienced team with a better understanding of quality requirements.
feedbacks: Reducing scope is a last resort.
Issuing formal warnings is not the best approach.
This is the best first step.
Reassigning the team is a premature action.
questions.explanation: The project manager must review and adjust the quality control process and work with the team to understand the causes of poor quality.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the PRINCE2 principle of ‘Manage by Exception’?
answers: Project teams are empowered to make decisions as required without consulting the project manager.
Project managers have the authority to change project plans at their own discretion.
Project boards will only become involved if the project has deviated outside of agreed tolerance levels.
Project boards are involved in all aspects of project management from start to finish.
feedbacks: Team empowerment is not the focus of this principle.
Unlimited authority to project managers is not a feature of this principle.
This correctly describes manage by exception.
Constant project board involvement is not a feature of this principle.
questions.explanation: ‘Manage by Exception’ delegates authority to the project manager to deliver within agreed tolerances, and the project board only intervenes if deviations occur.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the main purpose of the ‘Communication Management Approach’ document?
answers: To document and manage all of the project's risks and potential threats.
To provide a high-level summary of the project’s overall scope and objectives.
To provide a formal plan for managing project communications with all stakeholders.
To document and control all changes to the project’s agreed timelines and deliverables.
feedbacks: Risks and threats are not the focus of the communications approach.
Scope and objectives are separate to the communications approach.
This is the main purpose of the communications approach.
Changes to timelines are managed separately.
questions.explanation: The ‘Communication Management Approach’ provides a strategy for how information will be shared with all stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle, and outlines who will receive the information and how often.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of ‘Product-Based Planning’?
answers: To ensure that project plans are structured to meet stakeholder requirements.
To ensure that project plans are focused on the project’s deliverables and required outputs.
To ensure that project plans are focused on risk management and the mitigation of all potential threats.
To ensure that project plans are focused on the resources required to complete project tasks effectively.
feedbacks: Stakeholder engagement is not the main focus of this type of planning.
This describes the main purpose of product based planning.
Risk management is a separate process.
Resource management is not the main focus of this type of planning.
questions.explanation: ‘Product-Based Planning’ focuses all project planning around the products that will be delivered and ensures that project activities are planned around product creation.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing significant delays and is running considerably behind schedule. What is the best first action for the project board to take?
answers: Immediately terminate the project to avoid any further losses being incurred.
Demand that the project team work additional hours to make up the lost time.
Review the current project plans and identify the causes of the delays.
Reduce the scope of the project to ensure that at least part of the project is delivered on time.
feedbacks: Termination before analysis is not a good approach.
Demanding additional work might not solve the issues.
Reviewing the project plans is the correct first step.
Scope reduction without review is not good practice.
questions.explanation: The project board should review the project plans to fully understand the reasons for the delays prior to taking further action.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role of the ‘Project Manager’ in a PRINCE2 project?
answers: To provide all of the required resources to complete the project effectively.
To manage and control all project activity and resource allocation.
To create the project’s plans and monitor the projects performance against them.
To manage and mitigate all of the risks and issues that the project may face.
feedbacks: Providing resources is not the project manager's role.
Activity and resource allocation are managed by the project manager.
Planning and monitoring are key responsibilities of the project manager.
Risk and issue management are key to a project manager role.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Manager’ has a wide range of responsibilities, but is not responsible for providing the required resources to complete the project.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary purpose of the ‘Project Support’ role?
answers: To make key strategic decisions about the project's direction.
To manage the project’s budget and expenditure and track financial performance.
To provide specialist technical knowledge and guidance to the project team.
To provide project management, administrative and planning support to the project team.
feedbacks: Strategic decisions are made by the project board.
Budget management is the responsibility of the project executive.
Technical guidance is provided by other roles on the project.
This describes the purpose of the project support role.
questions.explanation: ‘Project Support’ provides a variety of administrative, planning and project management functions that ensure the team and manager are able to perform their roles effectively and efficiently.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the ‘Exception Plan’?
answers: To document the overall financial performance and expenditure of the project.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, which document should the Project Manager use to formally communicate project progress to the Project Board?
answers: The Risk Register.
The Issue Register.
The Highlight Report.
The Lessons Learned Report.
feedbacks: The risk register records risks, not overall progress.
The issue register records issues, not overall progress.
The Highlight report contains progress information.
Lessons learned is recorded post project.
questions.explanation: The 'Highlight Report' provides a summary of progress, and is used by the Project Manager to keep the board informed.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is running over budget, and the project board needs to make a decision on how to proceed. What should they do first?
answers: Reduce the project scope immediately to minimize overspending.
Review the business case, and assess whether the project is still viable.
Instruct the Project Manager to cut resources and reduce project quality.
Demand the project team completes the project regardless of cost.
feedbacks: Scope reduction is premature.

Cutting resources and quality may compromise the project outcome.
Demanding project completion regardless of cost is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: Reviewing the business case will help the project board determine whether the project is still worth the investment.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the main responsibility of the 'Change Authority'?
answers: To identify and record potential project risks.
To manage the team dynamics and interpersonal relationships.
To make decisions on project change requests.
To ensure that project benefits are being achieved.
feedbacks: Identifying risks is not the role of the change authority.
Team dynamics are not the concern of the change authority.
This is the main responsibility of the change authority.
Benefit realisation is not the role of the change authority.
questions.explanation: The 'Change Authority' is responsible for reviewing and approving change requests during the project.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is nearing the end of its current stage and the Project Manager is planning the end stage review. What should they do first?
answers: Update the project plan for the next stage of the project.
Review the project performance and prepare an end stage report.
Start drafting a formal project closure report.
Request input from the project team for the end stage assessment.
feedbacks: Updating the plan is premature.

Starting a closure report is premature.
Requesting team input is part of the process, not the first step.
questions.explanation: The project manager must review the stage and generate the end stage report to present to the project board.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a core component of the PRINCE2 'Risk Management Approach'?
answers: Risk identification and assessment.
Risk response planning and implementation.
Risk monitoring and review.
Risk impact calculations for business benefits.
feedbacks: Risk identification and assessment are core components.
Risk responses are part of this process.
Monitoring and review is essential for risk management.
Business benefits calculations are not directly linked to the risk management approach.
questions.explanation: Risk management focuses on identifying risks and documenting their likelihood and impact on a project, business benefits are not part of this process.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing conflicts between project team members. How should the Project Manager address this issue?
answers: Ignore the issue and let the team work it out without project manager intervention.
Issue a formal warning to all team members involved in the conflict.
Meet with the team to understand the conflict, and facilitate a resolution.
Replace all team members involved in the conflict with new resources.
feedbacks: Ignoring a conflict will cause it to fester.
Issuing a formal warning is premature.
Working with the team to resolve is best practice.
Replacing team members is a last resort.
questions.explanation: Project Managers must engage with their project team to resolve issues and conflict to maintain morale and productivity.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the 'Project Initiation Document (PID)'?
answers: To document and track all of the project’s risk events.
To guide the project team on the day to day execution of tasks.
To establish a baseline for how the project will be managed and delivered.
To capture the lessons learned throughout the project life cycle.
feedbacks: Risk events are documented elsewhere.
Guiding the project team is not the primary purpose of the PID.
This is the primary purpose of the PID.
Lessons learned are recorded post project, and not during initiation.
questions.explanation: The PID is used to establish all key information about the project in one document, and is used as the definitive authority for the project's management.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the PRINCE2 principle of 'Learn from Experience'?
answers: Project teams must be able to implement every recommendation they have ever received.
Project managers should rely on their previous experience to guide project delivery.
Lessons must be sought and recorded for use on current and future projects.
Project teams must be able to solve every project issue without any external help.
feedbacks: Implementing every recommendation regardless of value is not correct.
Relying only on previous experience is not sufficient.
This is the correct explanation of the learn from experience principle.
Solving all issues without external help is unrealistic.
questions.explanation: The 'Learn from Experience' principle provides guidance on how to document and share project experiences, in order that future projects can benefit.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has been running for some time and the project manager reports that there is a risk that the project is unlikely to achieve its full benefits. What should the project board do first?
answers: Reduce the project scope to ensure some of the benefits are realised.
Demand that the project manager produces a plan to deliver full benefits.
Review the business case to ensure the project is still worth continuing.
Terminate the project immediately to avoid further losses.
feedbacks: Reducing scope is a last resort.
Demanding the project manager produces a plan is unrealistic.
Reviewing the business case is the first appropriate action.
Termination without investigation is a drastic step.
questions.explanation: The project board must ensure the project still provides value, as determined by the business case. The most appropriate first step is to review it, prior to taking further action.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a role of the Project Board in a PRINCE2 project?
answers: To authorize all changes to the project’s baseline.
To ensure project activity remains within agreed tolerances.
To provide day-to-day direction and task assignment to the project team.
To provide the financial resources needed to complete the project.
feedbacks: The project board is responsible for authorizing changes to baseline.
This is a project board responsibility.
Day to day direction and task assignment are the role of the project manager.
The project board, and executive, provide funding to the project.
questions.explanation: The Project Board provides direction and governance for the project but does not perform day-to-day task management.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term 'Product-Based Planning' refer to?
answers: The process of managing the project’s financial budget.
The process of ensuring all project products meet quality standards.
The process of planning all activities based on the project’s desired outcomes and products.
The process of ensuring that all stakeholders are fully involved in the project.
feedbacks: Budgeting is separate to product-based planning.
Product quality is linked to project outputs and specifications, not planning.
This is the main goal of product based planning.
Stakeholder engagement is not the goal of product based planning.
questions.explanation: 'Product-Based Planning' focuses on the creation of project plans that are based on the end result, ensuring everything is structured to deliver the desired product(s).

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team is having difficulty managing dependencies between different work packages. What should the project manager do FIRST to address this issue?
answers: Ask the project board to reduce the project scope, to simplify the work.
Implement a strict reporting system to monitor progress.
Meet with the teams to clearly understand the dependencies and plan a solution.
Reassign the team members between work packages to allow more balanced workloads.
feedbacks: Reducing scope is a last resort.
Strict reporting will not resolve dependencies.
Understanding and planning a solution is the correct course of action.
Reassigning team members will not address dependencies.
questions.explanation: Understanding and planning work package dependencies is essential for the project to maintain progress and is the project manager’s responsibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST description of a ‘Project Initiation Document (PID)’?
answers: A document that tracks all identified risks throughout the project.
A document that contains all management information required to initiate and manage a project.
A document that contains all user requirements and product specifications.
A document that is used to communicate project progress to all stakeholders.
feedbacks: Risks are recorded in the risk register, not the PID.
This accurately describes the PID.
User requirements are recorded in other documents, not the PID.
Progress is documented elsewhere, not the PID.
questions.explanation: The PID consolidates all key management information about the project and sets the scene for how the project will be managed.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the 'Managing Product Delivery' process?
answers: To ensure products are delivered on time and within budget.
To control work and ensure that the work packages are delivered correctly.
To provide project direction and manage overall project strategy.
To manage and control project risks and issues.
feedbacks: This is a goal, but not the primary purpose.
This is the main objective of the managing product delivery process.
Project direction is handled in the directing a project process.
Managing risk is part of the managing a stage boundary process.
questions.explanation: 'Managing Product Delivery' is about controlling how specialist work is completed and ensuring that project products are delivered.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has recently experienced a serious unforeseen technical issue that could impact all future project progress. According to PRINCE2, which action should the Project Board take FIRST?
answers: Ask the project manager to provide a new plan which ignores the technical issues and continues.
Immediately close the project and stop all further spending.
Evaluate the impact of the technical issue on the business case and viability.
Instruct the project manager to resolve the issue without any consultation.
feedbacks: Ignoring the issue is not appropriate.
Closure without a full review is premature.
This is the most appropriate first action.
Ignoring the project manager is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: Reassessing the business case will ensure that project objectives and scope remain valid after a serious technical issue.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of an 'Issue' within a PRINCE2 project?
answers: An event that has already happened.
A threat to project timelines and budget.
A problem that requires a solution or intervention.
An event that impacts a project in a negative way.
feedbacks: This is a key characteristic of an issue.
This describes a risk, not an issue.
An issue is a problem requiring intervention.
Issues have a negative impact on the project.
questions.explanation: A risk is a potential event, whereas an issue is an event that has already happened.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term 'Exception' refer to?
answers: A request to change the project's objectives or goals.
A plan to reduce the overall project timeline or budget.
A situation where project activity has deviated beyond its predefined tolerances.
A highly successful project outcome that exceeds expectations.
feedbacks: Change requests are managed using the change control process.
A plan to reduce timeline is not an exception.
This is the core definition of an exception.
A successful outcome is not an exception.
questions.explanation: An 'Exception' is a situation where the project has breached its predefined tolerances in terms of cost, scope or timescale.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is suffering from poor communication between the project team members. What is the BEST course of action the project manager should take FIRST?
answers: Provide all project team members with a full copy of the project management plan.
Meet with the project team to understand the specific issues.
Reassign team members to create better working relationships.
Publicly reprimand all team members that are not communicating sufficiently.
feedbacks: The project plan is not a tool for communication.
Meeting the team to understand issues is best practice.
Reassigning teams is a last resort.
Public reprimand is not good practice.
questions.explanation: Meeting the project team will assist the project manager in understanding the cause of the poor communication.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important to include in a 'Work Package' for a PRINCE2 project?
answers: The overall project budget.
The project’s risk register.
A clear description of the product to be delivered and the activities required.
The project’s communication management plan.

The risk register is not a feature of the work package.
This is a key element of a work package.
The communication plan is a separate project document.
questions.explanation: A 'Work Package' contains the details of a specific deliverable and the tasks required to achieve the goal.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has just completed, and some of the promised benefits have not been achieved. What should the Project Board do FIRST?
answers: Ignore the unmet benefits and celebrate the project completion.
Ask the project manager to re-plan and deliver the benefits by extending the project.
Review the original business case to assess whether the project is still viable.
Immediately close the project to prevent further wastage of time and resources.

Extending the project is not best practice without analysis.
Reviewing the business case is the most appropriate first step.
Closing immediately is a drastic step.
questions.explanation: Reassessing the business case ensures that the board is fully aware of the project status and can make a considered decision.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary responsibility of the 'Senior User' on the Project Board?

To define all technical specifications for the project products.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the primary purpose of the 'End Stage Report'?
answers: To provide a status update on overall project progress.
To seek authorization to start the next stage.
To document the lessons learned during the stage.
To manage any changes to the project’s scope.

Lessons learned are recorded elsewhere.
Managing changes is not the function of the end stage report.
questions.explanation: The 'End Stage Report' provides a summary of stage performance and the basis for the project board to authorize the next stage of the project.

questions.question: A Project Manager in a PRINCE2 project is having difficulty getting team members to commit to deadlines for task completion. What is the BEST course of action for the Project Manager to take first?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key component of the PRINCE2 'Progress' theme?

Reporting on project progress to stakeholders.
Managing deviations from project baselines.
Defining the quality criteria for the products to be delivered.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing conflict between the project team and external stakeholders. What is the BEST approach for the Project Manager to take?

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a PRINCE2 'Highlight Report'?

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the purpose of the 'Change Theme'?

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST description of the PRINCE2 principle of 'Manage by Stages'?

Review the original Business Case to evaluate if it’s still valid and achievable.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'Risk Register'?

To record and assess all potential threats and opportunities that the project could face.
To record all lessons learned from previous projects.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key purpose of the 'Communication Management Approach' document in PRINCE2?

The Project Initiation Document (PID).
The Lessons Learned Report.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of the 'Senior Supplier' in a PRINCE2 project?

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has just completed a stage, and the Project Board needs to make a decision about whether to proceed. Which of the following should the Project Manager provide to the Project Board to assist with this decision?

questions.question: A project team is struggling to meet its deadlines, what is the BEST approach for a PRINCE2 project manager to take first?
answers: Publicly reprimand the team to make them work harder.
Reduce the scope of the project to reduce the workload.
Meet with the project team to review timelines and understand the cause of the issues.

Scope reduction is not the best first action.
Meeting the team is the best first step.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of the PRINCE2 ‘Quality’ theme?

Meeting project stakeholders quality expectations.
Tracking the project’s cost against its budget.
Ensuring that project products are free of errors.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary purpose of the 'Project Plan'?

To define how, when, and by whom the project’s objectives will be delivered.
To record the project's risk assessment process and mitigation plans.
feedbacks: The vision and scope is in the project brief, not the plan.

Risk assessment is not a feature of the project plan.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term ‘Tolerance’ specifically define?
answers: The acceptable level of risk that the project board will accept.
The level of management intervention that is required during a stage.
The limits of deviation from the agreed project baselines.
The amount of additional funding that can be made available to the project.

Management intervention is not part of the tolerance.
This is the purpose of tolerance.
Additional funds are not defined by tolerances.
questions.explanation: Tolerances define the acceptable deviation from agreed baselines in terms of cost, scope, time, benefits and quality.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing a serious issue that has the potential to affect the overall project outcome. What action should the project manager take FIRST?
answers: Attempt to resolve the issue independently, without consulting other parties.
Immediately communicate the issue to the project board, and request guidance.
Reassign team members and allow them to attempt to solve the issue.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical item contained in a PRINCE2 'Work Package'?
answers: A clear description of the work to be completed.
The quality criteria the products must meet.
The technical skills needed to complete the work.
The project’s risk register and mitigation plans.
feedbacks: A description of the work is key to the work package.
Quality criteria are needed within the work package.
Skills needed to complete the work is part of the work package.
The risk register is separate from the work package.
questions.explanation: The ‘Work Package’ contains the details of the tasks that need to be performed, but does not contain the overall project risks.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary responsibility of the 'Project Assurance' team?
answers: To provide specialist technical guidance to project teams.
To monitor project performance and adherence to governance.
To manage the day to day running of the project.
To ensure that project benefits are being realised.
feedbacks: Specialist guidance is not part of the project assurance responsibility.
Monitoring project adherence is the core purpose of project assurance.
Day to day running is the role of the project manager.
Benefit realisation is the responsibility of the project board.
questions.explanation: 'Project Assurance' provides an objective view of project governance and performance, ensuring that best practices are followed.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the ‘Issue Register’?
answers: To manage the project’s budget and financial performance.
To track the project’s overall progress against its plans.
To record all requests to change the project scope or product requirements.
To document and manage all issues that have already occurred during the project.
feedbacks: Budgets are managed in project finances.
Project progress is managed in the highlight reports.
Change requests are managed separately.
This is the main purpose of the issue register.
questions.explanation: The ‘Issue Register’ is used to document and track all problems and issues that have already occurred during the project lifecycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key feature of the PRINCE2 'Plans' theme?
answers: Defining how the project will deliver its desired products.
Managing the project’s resource allocations and schedules.
Defining how the project will manage its risks and issues.
Defining the project timelines and overall milestones.
feedbacks: Product delivery is a key part of the plans theme.
Resource allocations are managed in the plans theme.
Risk management is covered by the risk theme, not plans.
Timelines and milestones are defined by the plans theme.
questions.explanation: The ‘Plans’ theme defines how the project will achieve its goals, and manages resource allocation and timelines but it does not manage risks.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the BEST approach for a project manager to handle a change request that will have a significant impact on project cost and timelines?
answers: Ignore the change request to protect the project's baseline from change.
Immediately implement the change request to please the stakeholders.
Assess the impact, and make a decision to approve or reject without project board approval.
Record the change request, assess the impact, and seek Project Board approval.
feedbacks: Ignoring changes is not best practice.
Immediate implementation is not correct practice.
The project manager does not have authority to approve changes.
This is the best approach.
questions.explanation: All change requests that could affect project scope, cost, or timescale must be formally managed and approved by the Project Board.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team member is refusing to accept direction from the project manager and disrupting project flow. What is the first action the project manager should take?
answers: Issue a formal warning to the team member.
Reassign the team member to a less critical task.
Meet with the team member and attempt to understand the issue.
Ignore the team member and hope they will change their behaviour.
feedbacks: A formal warning is premature.
Reassigning is a drastic step.
Understanding the issue is the correct first step.
Ignoring a problem is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: Project Managers must attempt to understand the reasons for conflict and behaviour issues with their teams, and take action to improve communication and efficiency.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term 'Baseline' define?
answers: The minimum acceptable quality standard for project deliverables.
The detailed budget and expenditure for the overall project.
The agreed parameters, plan, and goals that the project will work to.
The lessons learned from previous projects.
feedbacks: Minimum quality levels are defined in product descriptions.
Budgets are tracked in project finances, not the baseline.
This is the main purpose of the baseline.
Lessons learned are recorded in a lessons learned report.
questions.explanation: The project 'Baseline' contains the agreed plans for cost, timescales, scope, and provides a point of reference for project monitoring and control.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing a sudden and unforeseen issue that requires urgent action. Which of the following steps should be undertaken FIRST by the Project Manager?
answers: Attempt to resolve the issue using resources available to the project team.
Contact the Project Board and provide a detailed summary of the issue and its potential impacts.
Re-allocate resources from other parts of the project to solve the issue.
Ignore the issue and continue with the project as planned in the hope that it is resolved.
feedbacks: Trying to resolve without authorization is not the best approach.
Contacting the board and providing a summary is the best step.
Reallocating resources without authorization is not correct practice.
Ignoring the issue is not best practice.
questions.explanation: In the event of a serious issue, the project manager should immediately inform the project board, and provide a detailed explanation of the problem.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate description of the PRINCE2 'Benefits Management Plan'?
answers: A document that details the process for managing the project's budget and financial performance.
A document that details the technical specifications and functions for all products to be delivered by the project.
A document that identifies the expected benefits, how they will be measured, and when they will be realized.
A document that outlines the approach for managing changes to the project’s scope and requirements.
feedbacks: Budget management is not included in the benefits management plan.
Product specifications are included in the product descriptions.
This is the main purpose of the benefits management plan.
Change management is not the function of the benefits management plan.
questions.explanation: The 'Benefits Management Plan' outlines how the project's benefits will be measured, and the processes and timing of their realization.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary purpose of the 'Directing a Project' process?
answers: To control day to day activities and deliver products.
To provide overall direction and governance for the project.
To manage and track the project’s progress and performance.
To ensure that project products meet defined quality requirements.
feedbacks: Day to day activities are managed in the 'Managing Product Delivery' process.
This is the key objective of the 'Directing a Project' process.
Project progress is tracked in the 'Controlling a Stage' process.
Product quality is managed separately using the quality theme.
questions.explanation: The ‘Directing a Project’ process provides high level guidance and governance to the project and ensures that it remains on track.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing conflict between various stakeholders due to a lack of communication, what is the first action a project manager should take?
answers: Send all stakeholders the project plans and hope that this will resolve the conflict.
Publicly reprimand all stakeholders for the lack of communication.
Review the Communication Management Plan and implement its strategies.
Allow the stakeholders to resolve the issue themselves without intervention.
feedbacks: Sending the plan does not address the issue.
Public reprimands are not good practice.
Implementing the communication plan is the best course of action.
Allowing self-resolution is not good management.
questions.explanation: The 'Communication Management Plan' is designed to manage communication with stakeholders, and should be the first point of reference for this situation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key aspect of the PRINCE2 principle of 'Continued Business Justification'?
answers: Ensuring the project remains aligned to its strategic objectives.
Regularly reviewing the project's business case.
Assessing the project's benefits throughout the project lifecycle.
Ensuring the project delivers its technical specifications, regardless of the cost or benefit.
feedbacks: Ensuring strategic alignment is essential for continued business justification.
Reviewing the business case is essential for continued business justification.
Regularly assessing benefits is essential for continued business justification.
Technical specifications must meet business needs and objectives and cannot be independent of cost/benefit.
questions.explanation: The principle of 'Continued Business Justification' requires that a project continues to represent a sound business investment throughout its lifecycle.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the primary purpose of the 'Exception Plan'?
answers: To detail all of the technical specifications for project deliverables.
To provide a new plan when a project is outside of its agreed tolerances.
To record all lessons learned at the end of a project stage.
To detail the communication strategies for all stakeholders.
feedbacks: Technical specifications are captured in product descriptions, not exception plans.
This is the key objective of the exception plan.
Lessons learned are recorded separately.
Stakeholder communications are managed in the communication plan.
questions.explanation: The ‘Exception Plan’ details the revised approach to completing the project, when it has deviated from its agreed tolerances.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the FIRST action a Project Manager should take when a major risk becomes highly likely?
answers: Attempt to implement the risk mitigation strategy without further discussion.
Escalate the risk to the Project Board with options for the correct response.
Reassign team members to find a solution to the issue, and then contact the project board.

Escalating the risk to the project board is the correct first action.
Reassigning team members is not appropriate.
Ignoring risks is not appropriate.
questions.explanation: Project Managers must escalate high-risk issues to the project board, to ensure they can make appropriate decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of a PRINCE2 'Work Package'?
answers: A clear description of the work to be completed.
The project’s overall business case and financial justification.
The quality standards and criteria that must be met.
The acceptance criteria for the products delivered.
feedbacks: A description of work is required in the work package.
Business justification is a separate project deliverable and is not part of the work package.
Quality standards are required in the work package.
Acceptance criteria are required in the work package.
questions.explanation: The ‘Work Package’ contains the details for a specific piece of work, and not the overall justification for the project.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is consistently over budget and the project board has identified that benefits are unlikely to be met. What is the best first action for the project board to take?
answers: Immediately close the project to reduce financial exposure.
Instruct the project manager to make changes to reduce costs regardless of impact.
Review the original business case to assess viability and return on investment.

Reviewing the business case is the most appropriate first step.

questions.explanation: The Project Board must review the business case to ensure the project remains viable and is worth the investment.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'Lessons Learned Report'?
answers: To document all of the project’s financial transactions.
To outline the project’s overall communication strategy.
To share knowledge and experiences gained from the project.
To provide a detailed analysis of all risks and issues faced during the project.
feedbacks: Financial transactions are not part of the lessons learned process.
The communications strategy is documented separately.
This is the purpose of the lessons learned report.
Risks and issues are tracked in the risk and issue registers.
questions.explanation: The ‘Lessons Learned Report’ is used to document project experiences and findings to provide information for future projects.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary responsibility of the ‘Project Executive’ on the Project Board?

To represent the interests of the users and stakeholders.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is consistently underperforming and the project manager is struggling to control the project. What action should the project board take FIRST?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid component of the PRINCE2 'Project Initiation Document' (PID)?

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'End Stage Report'?

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the purpose of the 'Change Theme'?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical use of the PRINCE2 'Lessons Learned Report'?

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the purpose of the 'Change Theme'?

To ensure that the correct resources are available to complete the project.
To effectively manage the risks that arise during the project.
To manage changes to the project’s scope and requirements.

Resource allocation is not managed by the change theme.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST description of the PRINCE2 principle of 'Manage by Stages'?

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'Risk Register'?

To record and assess all potential threats and opportunities that the project could face.
To record all lessons learned from previous projects.

questions.explanation: The 'Risk Register' is used to record all potential risks and opportunities, along with their assessments and possible responses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key purpose of the 'Communication Management Approach' document in PRINCE2?

To define how the project will communicate with external suppliers.

The Issue Register.
The Project Initiation Document (PID).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of the 'Senior Supplier' in a PRINCE2 project?

questions.question: A project team is struggling to meet its deadlines, what is the BEST approach for a PRINCE2 project manager to take first?

The limits of deviation from the agreed project baselines.
