questions.explanation: The 'Focus on Products' principle ensures that project plans are based around the required deliverables and that all activity is structured to meet the end objective.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the MAIN responsibility of the 'Project Assurance' role?
answers: To manage the project's financial resources and ensure best value for money.
To provide an independent overview and monitor project progress and compliance.
To manage the day to day activities of the project team.
To provide specialist technical expertise and guidance to the project team.
feedbacks: Managing finances is the responsibility of the project executive.
This is the role of project assurance.
Day to day management is the responsibility of the project manager.
Technical guidance is provided by the senior supplier.
questions.explanation: ‘Project Assurance’ provides an independent assessment of the project’s performance, and ensures compliance with processes and governance.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the purpose of the 'End Project Report'?
answers: To provide a summary of lessons learned during the course of the project.
To seek approval from the Project Board to close the project.
To formally evaluate the project performance and outcomes against the original goals and objectives.
To provide a detailed description of the technical specifications for the products to be delivered.
feedbacks: Lessons learned are recorded in the Lessons Learned Report, not the End Project Report.
Seeking approval is only one component of the end project report.
This is the correct description of the End Project Report.
Technical specifications are documented elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The ‘End Project Report’ provides a formal summary of the project, and evaluates performance against the original objectives and expected benefits.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project has a new project manager who has not worked on a PRINCE2 project before. What should the project board do FIRST?
answers: Provide the new project manager with a copy of the project plan and expect them to implement it.
Instruct the project manager to watch experienced members of the team to learn their role.
Provide a full briefing to the project manager and a copy of the Project Initiation Document (PID).
Reassign the project to another project manager with more relevant experience.
feedbacks: Providing the plan is a good step, but not the only one.
Learning by observation is not a good way to learn PRINCE2.
Providing the PID is the most appropriate first step.
Reassigning the project is a last resort.
questions.explanation: A detailed briefing and a copy of the Project Initiation Document will provide the project manager with all of the essential information to manage the project effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of the PRINCE2 ‘Progress’ theme?
answers: Monitoring project timelines against the agreed schedule.
Measuring the performance of a project against its planned objectives.
Managing project resources to maximize productivity and efficiency.
Providing regular updates on project progress to stakeholders.
feedbacks: Monitoring timelines is part of the progress theme.
Measuring performance is a key feature of the progress theme.
Managing resources is not the core focus of this theme.
Providing regular updates is key to the progress theme.
questions.explanation: The 'Progress' theme ensures project activity is monitored and reported against the plans, but does not directly manage resources,

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the purpose of the 'Exception Plan'?
answers: To describe all potential risks and propose methods of mitigating them.
To document all lessons learned during the project for future use.
To provide a new plan for the project when its tolerances have been breached.
To outline the strategy and methods used for communicating with stakeholders.
feedbacks: Risk management is not the purpose of an exception plan.
Lessons learned are not part of the exception plan.
This is the correct definition of an exception plan.
Stakeholder communication is separate to the exception plan.
questions.explanation: The 'Exception Plan' is designed to provide a new way to achieve project objectives, when the project has gone outside of its agreed parameters.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what does the term 'Work Package' specifically define?
answers: The complete financial budget and plan for the whole project.
A detailed list of all the project risks and responses.
A set of information detailing the work required to create a specific project product.
The overall communication strategy and plan for all project stakeholders.
feedbacks: The project's budget is a separate document.
Risks and responses are included in the risk register.
This is the correct definition of a work package.
The communications strategy is separate from the work package.
questions.explanation: A 'Work Package' details the work required to deliver a specific product, and is given to the team who will perform the work.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project is experiencing a high level of staff turnover and new team members are unfamiliar with project processes. What action should the project manager take FIRST?
answers: Demand that all new team members complete the work regardless of familiarity with process.
Reassign the project to a new project manager with experience of managing new teams.
Review the project’s training and induction process and improve this to support new members.
Ignore the problem and expect team members to learn by observation.
feedbacks: Demanding new staff members complete work without support is not appropriate.
Reassigning to a new project manager is premature.
This is the most appropriate first step.
Ignoring the problem is not good project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager must review and improve the induction process to ensure all new team members are appropriately trained and understand the project management process.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical element of a PRINCE2 ‘Product Description’?
answers: The specific purpose and function of the product.
The quality criteria that the product must adhere to.
A list of all of the tasks that must be completed to create the product.
The skills required to create the product.
feedbacks: Product purpose is included in the description.
Quality standards are described in the product description.
Task lists are part of work packages, not the product description.
Skills required to create the product are part of the product description.
questions.explanation: The 'Product Description' details the characteristics of the product, but does not include a detailed list of the tasks required to create it.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the PRIMARY responsibility of the ‘Project Executive’ on the Project Board?
answers: To ensure that project products meet all required quality standards.
To provide the necessary financial resources and ensure value for money.
To manage the project's risk register and issue register.
To manage the day to day activities of the project team.
feedbacks: Product quality is not the responsibility of the project executive.
This is the main responsibility of the project executive.
Risk and issue management is not the responsibility of the project executive.
Day to day management is the responsibility of the project manager.
questions.explanation: The ‘Project Executive’ provides funding for the project, and ensures that it remains a worthwhile investment and will deliver value for money.

questions.question: In a PRINCE2 project, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the ‘Issue Register’?
answers: To track and manage all project risks and threats.
To manage the project budget and financial performance.
To record all problems and concerns that have occurred during the project.
To provide project updates and information to project stakeholders.
feedbacks: Risks are managed in a separate risk register.
Budget and financial information is not managed in the issue register.

Stakeholder information is managed using the communication approach.
questions.explanation: The ‘Issue Register’ provides a record of all problems and concerns that have arisen during the project lifecycle.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the PRINCE2 principle of 'Manage by Stages'?
answers: Projects should be divided into small work packages that can be delegated to project teams.
Projects should be managed as a single phase to allow maximum efficiency of resource allocation.
Projects should be managed as a series of distinct stages to enable control and review.
Project boards should delegate all decision-making authority to the project manager.
feedbacks: Work packages are separate to the stages.

questions.explanation: 'Manage by Stages' ensures that projects are broken into manageable phases with clear review points that enable stakeholders to make informed decisions about continuation.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the first action a project manager should take when a project deviates outside of its agreed tolerances?
answers: Immediately implement the predefined risk responses and try to recover the project.
Continue with the project as planned and expect the project to recover itself.
Immediately escalate the exception to the project board to review options.
Reassign team members and allocate new resources to complete the project.

questions.explanation: The project manager must escalate any deviation outside of tolerance to the project board for advice and guidance.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team member has refused to complete assigned tasks, what is the best first action for the project manager to take?
answers: Issue a formal warning to the team member for failing to complete the allocated work.
Reassign the work to a more willing and capable team member.
Meet with the team member to understand the reasons for their refusal.
Ignore the team member and hope that they will change their behaviour in the future.
feedbacks: Issuing a formal warning is premature.
Reassigning work is a last resort.
Understanding the reasons is the best first action.
Ignoring a problem is not good project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager should understand the reasons for the refusal of tasks prior to taking further action.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key function of the PRINCE2 'Progress' theme?
answers: Tracking project progress against its agreed schedule and plans.
Measuring project performance against its defined quality criteria.
Providing regular updates on the project’s status to all stakeholders.
Managing deviations from planned activity and implementing corrective actions.
feedbacks: Tracking progress is a core function of the progress theme.
Quality assessment is not the responsibility of the progress theme.
Project updates are a key feature of the progress theme.

questions.question: According to PRINCE2, what is the primary purpose of a ‘Work Package’?
answers: To provide details of all financial expenditure during the project lifecycle.
To provide details of all of the identified project risks and issues.
To provide clear instructions to a team on what work is required and how it should be completed.
To provide overall project objectives and scope to stakeholders.
feedbacks: Financial information is not part of a work package.
Risks and issues are documented separately.
This describes the work package correctly.
Project objectives are not part of the work package.
questions.explanation: The ‘Work Package’ provides clear instructions to a team or individual, for the tasks required to complete a specific deliverable.

answers: Managing stakeholder communications and their expectations of the project.
Managing and controlling all changes to project deliverables and their versions.
Managing project resources and allocating them efficiently to assigned tasks.
Managing the performance of the project team and improving team dynamics.

questions.explanation: ‘Configuration Management’ is about controlling and tracking the various deliverables and products that are created during the project lifecycle.

answers: Publicly reprimand the team members that are causing the problems.

Meet with all of the team members and try to understand the root causes of the issues.

Ignoring the issue is not good project management.
questions.explanation: The project manager must understand the cause of the problem prior to taking further action, and must work with the team to resolve issues and improve performance.

answers: To provide strategic guidance and direction to the project manager.
To approve all plans and deliverables for all stages of the project.
To provide day-to-day supervision and task management of the project team.
To provide all required financial resources for the project.

Approving plans is the responsibility of the project board.

answers: To provide a detailed budget and plan for managing project finances.
To specify all technical requirements and quality standards for project deliverables.
To document how, when and by whom project benefits will be measured and realized.
To document all project risks, issues and changes throughout the lifecycle.
feedbacks: Budget management is not the function of the benefits plan.

Risks, issues and changes are documented separately.
questions.explanation: The ‘Benefits Management Plan’ outlines the way in which the benefits of the project will be measured and realized by the business.

Instruct the project manager to make immediate changes to the project, to reduce the scope.
Reassess the business case to evaluate whether the project still provides a valid return on investment.
Demand that the project team work harder and faster, to complete the project within the new budget.

Reducing scope without analysis is not good practice.

answers: To allow the project team freedom to make their own decisions without guidance.

To provide limits on the amount that a project can deviate from its agreed plan.
To allow the project team to make changes as required to improve project outcomes.

questions.question: A PRINCE2 project team is failing to meet its agreed deadlines, what is the best first action for a project manager to take?
answers: Issue a formal warning to all team members for not completing work on time.
Reassign all tasks to a smaller and more experienced team.
Meet with the project team to understand the reasons for the missed deadlines.

answers: Making key decisions regarding the project’s strategic direction.

To ensure that changes to project baselines are controlled and managed appropriately.
